### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A14, A15 and A20 each ran exactly once in every trace (participation 100%); in the later window each appears in about 53 in 100 traces (106 of 200) and still at most once per trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- The three act as one block: every pair among them co-occurs in 100% of traces in both windows, always in the order A14 → A15 → A20, and in the later window all three are jointly absent in about 47 in 100 traces. [REL001, REL002, REL005]
- A36 and A21 still occur in every trace in both windows. Before, A36 was always followed by A14; in the later window its outgoing transitions lead to A14 in about 53 in 100 cases and directly to A21 in about 47 in 100. [DIR001, REL003, REL004]
- The step distance from A36 to A21 was always 4 before; in the later window it is 1 step in about 47 in 100 traces and 4 steps in the remaining 53 in 100. [LAG001]
- Co-occurrence of A36, and of A21, with each block activity fell from 100% to about 53%, with A36 or A21 now appearing without the block in about 47 in 100 traces. [REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009]
- A21's mean event position sits slightly earlier in the later window (about 0.43 vs 0.40 of the trace) with slightly more spread, consistent with shorter traces when the block is missing; positions are event ranks, not clock times. [POS001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the block A14 → A15 → A20, which always executed between A36 and A21 in the earlier window, became optional: in the later window it is skipped in about 47 in 100 traces, and A36 then leads directly to A21. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, LAG001]

The volume of qualifying items far exceeds what an unchanged process would produce: 15 control-flow items qualified against roughly 0.35 expected for the 71 tested units, and all items point to one underlying difference. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, POS001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, LAG001]

The hypothesis is shown directly and consistently: A36 gains a direct transition to A21 that was not observed before [DIR001], the A36-to-A21 distance shrinks from always 4 steps to 1 step in about 47% of traces [LAG001], and the block's participation falls from 100% to about 53% while A36 and A21 remain in all traces [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, REL003, REL004]. When present, the block still runs intact in the same internal order, so this is a skip of an existing block rather than a reordering or a shift of shares between always-present alternatives. [REL001, REL002, REL005]

Competing explanation: the evidence cannot distinguish a new per-trace skip choice from a changed mix of two pre-existing case types (one with the block, one without), since both windows are finite samples of 200 traces. [DIR001, LAG001, REL001]
